"'''All My Life'''" is a song recorded by American [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] duo [[K-Ci & JoJo]]. The song was written by Joel "JoJo" Hailey and Rory Bennett and produced by K-Ci & JoJo for the duo’s debut studio album, ''[[Love Always]]'' (1997). The song was released to airplay in January 1998 and was released physically on March 17, 1998, as the third single from the album through [[MCA Records]]. "All My Life" is an [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]] and [[Soul music|soul]] song. Music critics have claimed this as the duo's most successful song of their career.

"All My Life" was a commercial success, topping the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] for three consecutive weeks. It was certified [[RIAA certification|gold]] in the US and was the duo's longest-running number-one single of their career. "All My Life" performed well internationally, peaking at number one in Australia, the Netherlands, and New Zealand and entering the top 10 in eight other countries. It achieved platinum status in Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.

"All My Life" is a song recorded by American R&B duo K-Ci & JoJo. The song was written by Joel "JoJo" Hailey and Rory Bennett and produced by K-Ci & JoJo for the duo’s debut studio album, Love Always (1997). The song was released to airplay in January 1998 and was released physically on March 17, 1998, as the third single from the album through MCA Records. "All My Life" is an R&B and soul song. Music critics have claimed this as the duo's most successful song of their career.

"All My Life" was a commercial success, topping the US Billboard Hot 100 for three consecutive weeks. It was certified gold in the US and was the duo's longest-running number-one single of their career. "All My Life" performed well internationally, peaking at number one in Australia, the Netherlands, and New Zealand and entering the top 10 in eight other countries. It achieved platinum status in Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom.

In 1997, K-Ci & JoJo traveled to various [[recording studios]] in California and New York with multiple relatively unknown record producers for recording of their debut album, ''[[Love Always]]''.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.borders.com/online/store/TitleDetail?sku=008811161323 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120731185721/http://www.borders.com/online/store/TitleDetail?sku=008811161323 |url-status = dead|archive-date=July 31, 2012 |title=Love Always – K-Ci & JoJo – Compact Disc (UPC 0008811161323) |publisher=Borders |access-date=August 11, 2011 }}</ref> JoJo Hailey initially wrote the song, using his daughter as inspiration.<ref name="bare_url" /> "All My Life" was originally written by JoJo Hailey for a female artist on [[A&M Records]], but ultimately he decided to keep the song.<ref name="encyclopedia" /> "All My Life" was recorded at Audio Achievements in [[Torrance, California]].<ref name="bare_url_a">{{Cite magazine | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=aQ0EAAAAMBAJ | title=Production credits | magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] | publisher=[[Nielsen Business Media]] | date=April 25, 1998 | volume=110 | issn=0006-2510 | page=45 | issue=17}}</ref> Rory Bennett contributed on the song by helping the writing and the production.

In 1997, K-Ci & JoJo traveled to various recording studios in California and New York with multiple relatively unknown record producers for recording of their debut album, Love Always. JoJo Hailey initially wrote the song, using his daughter as inspiration. "All My Life" was originally written by JoJo Hailey for a female artist on A&M Records, but ultimately he decided to keep the song. "All My Life" was recorded at Audio Achievements in Torrance, California. Rory Bennett contributed on the song by helping the writing and the production.

sections.heading: Music and theme
sections.wikitext: "All My Life" is a slow-tempo [[love song]] ballad, performed in slow [[Groove (music)|groove]]. It is composed in the [[key (music)|key]] of [[D-flat major|D{{music|flat}} major]] and is set to 63 beats per minute in the time signature of [[Time signature|common time]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtdVPE.asp?ppn=MN0040067 | title=K-Ci & JoJo – All My Life Sheet Music (Digital Download) | work=Music Notes | date=July 3, 2001 | access-date=August 23, 2011}}</ref> "All My Life" has been classified as an [[Contemporary R&B|R&B]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://allmusic.com/album/love-always-r277564 | title=''Love Always'' – K-Ci & JoJo > Overview | work=Allmusic | publisher=Rovi Corporation | access-date=August 24, 2011}}</ref> and [[Soul music|soul]]<ref name="bare_url">{{Cite journal | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qwUDRnr2e-AC | pages=80, 82, 178 | title=K-Ci & JoJo: Music's Hottest Duo | journal=[[Ebony (magazine)|Ebony]] | publisher=Johnson Publishing Company | volume=53 | issue=12 | date=October 1998 | issn=0012-9011 | last=Kinnon | first=Joy Bennett}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=w0QqC0F-PH0C | title=The Bpm List: A Music Reference Guide for Mobile DJs |author1=Brusca, Donald |author2=Brusca, Donny | page=22 | year=2005 | publisher=LuLu | location=Staten Island, New York | isbn=978-1-4116-4211-9}}</ref> song.
sections.text: "All My Life" is a slow-tempo love song ballad, performed in slow groove. It is composed in the key of D{{music|flat}} major and is set to 63 beats per minute in the time signature of common time. "All My Life" has been classified as an R&B and soul song.

sections.heading: Release and reception
sections.wikitext:
"All My Life" was released as the third single from the album ''Love Always''. The song was released in the United States on March 17, 1998, as a [[CD single]].<ref name="usretail">{{cite magazine|title=Datu Faison's Rhythm Section|last=Faison|first=Datu|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|volume=110|issue=12|page=32|date=March 21, 1998|quote=On Tuesday (17), 'All My Life' by K-Ci & JoJo (MCA) hits stores...}}</ref> It was released on March 30, 1998, in Germany as a [[maxi single]].<ref name="germx">{{cite web | url=https://www.amazon.de/dp/B00000AFSK | title=All My Life: K-Ci & Jojo: Amazon.de: Musik | language=de | work=Amazon.de | access-date=August 24, 2011}}</ref> "[[Don't Rush (Take Love Slowly)]]" was included as the [[A-side and B-side|B-side]] on all copies. In many European countries, "All My Life" was released as a maxi single without a B-side, but contained a radio edit as well as two remixes.<ref name="sc_Australia_K-Ci & JoJo" /> On September 18, 2001, "All My Life" would be available to [[Music download|download digitally]] via the [[iTunes Store]], but "[[Tell Me It's Real]]" was included instead of "Don't Rush".<ref name="bare_url_b">{{cite web|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/all-my-life/id6338495?i=6338412 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121113131033/https://itunes.apple.com/us/album/all-my-life/id6338495?i=6338412 |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 13, 2012 |title=All My Life / Tell Me It's Real - Single by K-Ci & JoJo |publisher=[[iTunes]] |date=September 18, 2001 |access-date=June 14, 2014}}</ref>

The song was praised by music critics, who classify it as the duo's most successful song. Steve Heuy of [[AllMusic]] calls "All My Life" a "sweet ballad" and claims the song "broke them big".<ref>{{cite web | url=http://allmusic.com/artist/k-ci-jojo-p210589/biography | title=K-Ci & JoJo > Biography | work=[[AllMusic]] | publisher=Rovi Corporation | access-date=August 24, 2011}}</ref> ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine writer Aliya King wrote "All My Life" "cemented the duo's reputation as sensitive and soulful crooners."<ref>{{cite magazine | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tQ0EAAAAMBAJ&q=k-ci+%26+jojo+all+my+life&pg=PA65 | page=65 | title=MCA's K-Ci & JoJo Get 'Real' With Their Sophomore Set | magazine=Billboard | publisher=Nielsen Business Media | volume=111 | number=23 | issn=0006-2510 | date=June 5, 1999}}</ref> Gerald Martinez from ''[[New Sunday Times]]'' described it as "scintillating", noting that it "features some stunning vocal arrangements."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Gerald|last=Martinez|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=iZoWAAAAIBAJ|title=Dance fever for one and all|magazine=[[New Sunday Times]]|date=November 8, 1998|page=13|accessdate=October 21, 2021}}</ref> Ralph Tee from the ''[[Record Mirror]]'' Dance Update gave the song four out of five, adding, "The two [[Jodeci]] boys thrill with this urban beat ballad, strings and plonky piano intro making it a real show-stopping performance piece. Rich with the duo's own harmonies, it's one of those records you can really grow into."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=Ralph|last=Tee|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1998/Music-Week-1998-03-21.pdf|title=Hot Vinyl|magazine=[[Music Week]], in [[Record Mirror]] (Dance Update Supplemental Insert)|date=March 21, 1998|page=8|access-date=September 13, 2023}}</ref>
sections.text:
"All My Life" was released as the third single from the album Love Always. The song was released in the United States on March 17, 1998, as a CD single. It was released on March 30, 1998, in Germany as a maxi single. "Don't Rush (Take Love Slowly)" was included as the B-side on all copies. In many European countries, "All My Life" was released as a maxi single without a B-side, but contained a radio edit as well as two remixes. On September 18, 2001, "All My Life" would be available to download digitally via the iTunes Store, but "Tell Me It's Real" was included instead of "Don't Rush".

The song was praised by music critics, who classify it as the duo's most successful song. Steve Heuy of AllMusic calls "All My Life" a "sweet ballad" and claims the song "broke them big". Billboard magazine writer Aliya King wrote "All My Life" "cemented the duo's reputation as sensitive and soulful crooners." Gerald Martinez from New Sunday Times described it as "scintillating", noting that it "features some stunning vocal arrangements." Ralph Tee from the Record Mirror Dance Update gave the song four out of five, adding, "The two Jodeci boys thrill with this urban beat ballad, strings and plonky piano intro making it a real show-stopping performance piece. Rich with the duo's own harmonies, it's one of those records you can really grow into."

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
The single debuted on the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] at number 15.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yQ4EAAAAMBAJ|title=Billboard|date=March 28, 1998|publisher=Nielsen Business Media, Inc.|access-date=May 8, 2021|via=Google Books}}</ref> It reached the chart's top spot the following week.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ug4EAAAAMBAJ|title=Billboard|date=April 4, 1998|publisher=Nielsen Business Media, Inc.|access-date=May 8, 2021|via=Google Books}}</ref> The song stayed on the Hot 100 for 35 weeks.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.billboard.biz/bbbiz/charts/singles-chart-search|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101221021427/http://www.billboard.biz/bbbiz/charts/singles-chart-search|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 21, 2010|title=Chart search|website=Billboard.biz|quotation=Type "K-Ci" into Artist, "All My Life" into Single Title. Select "The Billboard Hot 100" from the Single Chart Name, "All Weeks (Artist or Title Required)" from date. Click "Submit"}}</ref> "All My Life" achieved success on other ''Billboard'' charts, including the [[Hot R&B Singles]] chart, peaking at number one, the [[Rhythmic (chart)|Rhythmic Top 40]] chart, peaking at number one, and the [[Adult Contemporary (chart)|Adult Contemporary]] chart, peaking at number 26.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://allmusic.com/album/love-always-r277564/charts-awards/billboard-single |title=Love Always - K-Ci & JoJo | Awards |website=AllMusic |date=June 17, 1997 |access-date=June 14, 2014}}</ref> It would also rank at number 98 on ''Billboard''{{'}}s Hot 100 decade-end chart.<ref name="1990sbb" />

Internationally, "All My Life" peaked inside the top 10 on multiple charts. It peaked at number two on the Australian [[ARIA Charts|ARIA Singles Chart]] and was certified platinum by the [[Australian Recording Industry Association]] (ARIA) for shipments of 70,000 units in Australia.<ref name=ARIA/> The song also peaked at number four on the Swedish [[Sverigetopplistan|Hitlistan]] chart and was certified gold by the [[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]] (IFPI).<ref name=GLF/> "All My Life" also peaked at number 12 in Austria,<ref name="sc_Austria_K-Ci & JoJo" /> number three in [[Flanders]],<ref name="sc_Flanders_K-Ci & JoJo" /> number 11 in [[Wallonia]],<ref name="sc_Wallonia_K-Ci & JoJo" /> number 43 in France,<ref name="sc_France_K-Ci & JoJo" /> number one in the Netherlands and New Zealand,<ref name="sc_Dutch100_K-Ci & JoJo" /><ref name="sc_New Zealand_K-Ci & JoJo" /> number two in Norway,<ref name="sc_Norway_K-Ci & JoJo" /> number four in Switzerland,<ref name="sc_Switzerland_K-Ci & JoJo" /> and number eight in the United Kingdom.<ref name="sc_UK_K-Ci & JoJo" />
sections.text:
The single debuted on the US Billboard Hot 100 at number 15. It reached the chart's top spot the following week. The song stayed on the Hot 100 for 35 weeks. "All My Life" achieved success on other Billboard charts, including the Hot R&B Singles chart, peaking at number one, the Rhythmic Top 40 chart, peaking at number one, and the Adult Contemporary chart, peaking at number 26. It would also rank at number 98 on Billboard{{'}}s Hot 100 decade-end chart.

Internationally, "All My Life" peaked inside the top 10 on multiple charts. It peaked at number two on the Australian ARIA Singles Chart and was certified platinum by the Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) for shipments of 70,000 units in Australia. The song also peaked at number four on the Swedish Hitlistan chart and was certified gold by the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI). "All My Life" also peaked at number 12 in Austria, number three in Flanders, number 11 in Wallonia, number 43 in France, number one in the Netherlands and New Zealand, number two in Norway, number four in Switzerland, and number eight in the United Kingdom.

sections.heading: Accolades
sections.wikitext: "All My Life" was nominated for multiple awards. At the [[41st Annual Grammy Awards|41st Grammy Awards]] in 1999, "All My Life" was nominated for [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocals|Best R&B Vocal Performance]] and [[Grammy Award for Best R&B Song|Best R&B Song]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.rockonthenet.com/archive/1999/grammys.htm | title=41st Annual Grammy Awards – 1991 | publisher=Rock On The Net | access-date=August 24, 2011}}</ref> The music video for the song was nominated for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best R&B Video|Best R&B Video]] at the [[1998 MTV Video Music Awards]], losing to [[Wyclef Jean]]'s "[[Gone till November]]".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rockonthenet.com/archive/1998/mtvvmas.htm |title=1998 MTV Video Music Awards |publisher=Rock On The Net |date=September 10, 1998 |access-date=June 14, 2014}}</ref>
sections.text: "All My Life" was nominated for multiple awards. At the 41st Grammy Awards in 1999, "All My Life" was nominated for Best R&B Vocal Performance and Best R&B Song. The music video for the song was nominated for Best R&B Video at the 1998 MTV Video Music Awards, losing to Wyclef Jean's "Gone till November".

sections.heading: Music video
sections.wikitext: The song's accompanying music video was directed by Lara M. Schwartz.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DXvMT_mVbqw|title=K-Ci & JoJo - All My Life|last=KCiAndJoJoVEVO|date=October 6, 2009|via=YouTube}}</ref> It begins by showing many of the people in the crowd, followed by a pianist playing the introduction. It eventually pans over K-Ci & JoJo as they begin singing into their microphones. Every so often, an outside scene of love will show up. Examples are of a teacher helping a student read, parents with a newborn baby, a woman giving a homeless man food, a lesbian couple laying in bed and talking, and a father with his daughter. In between these scenes, the camera pans over the stage, as well as the people in the crowd and the musicians. At the end, the camera shows a sunset and pans away.
